sponsor_question: For every shipped LLM system, is the output measurably good right now, and what does knowing that cost.

outcomes.name: Gated pass rate, per subject
outcomes.unit: % of scorable cases; program-level the minimum across billed subjects
outcomes.definition: For the latest run of each subject: cases that passed every gating characteristic ÷ cases that did not error (case-weighted — CaseResult.passed). Errored cases are excluded from the base and reported by error-rate. Program-level: the minimum across subjects with a model (billed); deterministic subjects are reported but do not set the minimum. A subject with no scorable cases is reported in the no-signal state, never 0 % or 100 %.

source.system: eval-store snapshot (RC1-301): one row per run
source.query: latest row per subject by started_at: passed, cases, errored, model

outcomes.stale_after: 7 days since the subject's last run
outcomes.so_what: A billed subject under 80 % on two consecutive measurements: freeze prompt changes on that repo until a run passes. A drop of more than 10 points between runs with the same prompt version: the model changed, pin it.

goodhart.gaming_path: Delete the hard cases, or flip a failing characteristic to advisory.
goodhart.counter: Gating case count and advisory share, reported beside it; a pass-rate rise with a case-count fall is flagged.

failure_modes: Survivorship: only subjects someone chose to run are in the latest-run set.
Denominator collapse: a subject with 20 scorable cases of 46 is on a small base; a two-case subject flips 50 points on one case.
A subject whose latest run is weeks old is carried as stale by measurement-freshness-days, not re-read as current.

outcomes.name: Real cost per run
outcomes.unit: USD per recorded run, trailing 28 days
outcomes.definition: (Org model spend as billed by the Anthropic cost report + the store's Heroku invoice prorated to the window) ÷ runs recorded in the trailing 28 days. Billed dollars only — nothing in the numerator comes from a price table. The org feed cannot be filtered to eval traffic, so the value is an upper bound on the program's true cost; the price-table attribution of the same window's runs is reported beside it, and the unattributable gap is the number to watch.

source.system: billing feeds (RC1-308): anthropic-costs (org cost report, Admin API key) and heroku-invoices (account invoices, Platform API)
source.query: sum the anthropic-costs daily buckets in the window; prorate the latest heroku invoice per-day times 28; divide by eval-store runs in the window

outcomes.stale_after: 3 days without a cost-report bucket, or 40 days past the latest invoice period
outcomes.so_what: Real spend above 3x the price-table attribution on two consecutive readings: find the unattributed traffic before trusting any per-run economics. A sustained rise with flat run counts means the measurement program is paying for something it is not measuring.

goodhart.gaming_path: Take many cheap runs to dilute the denominator, or stop running suites so the KPI reads broken instead of expensive.
goodhart.counter: Cost per verified case and measurement freshness travel beside it; a per-run fall with a per-case rise, or a freshness trip, is named in the brief.

failure_modes: Attribution: the org feed includes non-eval traffic (the drift digest, the briefs themselves), so the value overstates the program's own cost.
Invoice lag: the current Heroku period is still open, so proration leans on the latest period the API reports.
A quiet week divides real fixed spend over few runs and reads expensive without anything having changed.

leading.name: Measurement freshness
leading.unit: days since the last run, per billed subject; program-level the maximum
leading.definition: today − max(started_at) per billed subject (model not null); program-level the maximum. A subject never run is reported never-measured, not 0.

source.system: eval-store snapshot (RC1-301): one row per run

leading.stale_after: never — this KPI defines stale for the others; it is computed from timestamps and the clock
leading.so_what: Any billed subject over 7 days: the weekly brief names it and the ask is 'run it or retire it'. Over 21 days the subject is dropped from the pass-rate minimum and listed as unmeasured.

goodhart.gaming_path: Run a subject with one case to reset the clock — caught by the case count reported beside the pass rate.

failure_modes: All runs land when a human takes a measurement; CI never writes. A tree without this indicator reports a pass rate indefinitely off three days of data.
CI exercises the free subjects without writing, so a subject can be exercised yet look unmeasured here.

leads.mechanism: A regression in a subject that has not been run cannot appear in the pass rate; freshness bounds how old the 'current' quality reading is.

leading.name: Error rate
leading.unit: % of cases that produced nothing to score, per subject; program-level the maximum
leading.definition: From the latest run per subject: errored ÷ cases × 100. A run with no cases is no-signal, never 0 %. Program-level the maximum across subjects, with the subject named.

source.system: eval-store snapshot (RC1-301): one row per run
source.query: latest row per subject: errored, cases

leading.so_what: Error rate over 20 % on a subject: the decision is an infrastructure fix (key, fixture, timeout) before any quality conclusion is drawn from that subject; the brief says 'unmeasured', not a pass rate.

goodhart.gaming_path: Swallow exceptions so errors become failures or passes — a code-review matter, and visible as a pass-rate change on the same case set.

failure_modes: A subject where every case errors has a pass rate of 0/0: reported no-signal, never 0 % or 100 %.
Reflects only the last human-triggered run.

leads.mechanism: Errored cases leave the pass-rate base, making it smaller and more flattering; and errors are the harness breaking, which is a different fix from a prompt regression.
leads.lead_time: same run; the decision differs, which is why it is separate

leading.name: Cost per run, by model
leading.definition: Mean cost per run over the trailing 4 weeks, grouped by subject and model, shown with the run's case count so a change can be attributed to model, prompt or case set. Deterministic runs (no model) are excluded.

source.system: eval-store snapshot (RC1-301): one row per run
source.query: cost_usd, cases, subject, model, started_at per run in the window

leading.so_what: A (subject, model) pair costing more than 3× the cheapest model that has run the same subject: the decision is to move it.
failure_modes: model is null on deterministic subjects: excluded, reported as 'no model'.
The price table is maintained by hand; a missing price is a broken instrument, not a free run.

leads.mechanism: The model a subject runs on sets its per-run cost; a move to a dearer model shows here on the first run and in the unit cost only as the window fills.
leads.lead_time: up to the window length, 4 weeks

leading.name: Cost per verified case
leading.unit: USD per scored case (and $ per full sweep)
leading.definition: (model_spend + store_fixed_cost_prorated) ÷ cases_scored over a trailing 4-week window, where model_spend is the sum of run cost in the window, store_fixed_cost_prorated is the Postgres plan's monthly price × (window days ÷ 30), and cases_scored counts non-errored cases. Also reported as $ per full sweep: the cost of the latest run of every billed subject. A $0 billed run is a broken instrument, not a cheap run; where cost is absent it is recomputed from tokens × price and flagged.

source.system: eval-store snapshot (RC1-301): one row per run + Postgres plan billing
source.query: cost_usd, cases, errored, started_at per run in the window; the plan's fixed monthly price
source.cadence: per run; monthly for the plan price

leading.stale_after: 7 days (if no run lands in 7 days the numerator is only the fixed cost and the value is stale, not 'cost fell')
leading.so_what: If $ per verified case rises more than 50 % without a matching rise in cases or a deliberate model upgrade, the decision is model choice per subject; if a full sweep exceeds the ceiling, sweeps go fortnightly.

goodhart.gaming_path: Run the free subjects more often: cases up, spend flat, billed systems unmeasured.
goodhart.counter: measurement-freshness-days per billed subject, and the per-sweep figure, which free runs do not move.

failure_modes: A consumer that does not set cost_usd records $0 and the run renders as free.
The fixed cost dominates at low volume: the unit cost is mostly how often anyone runs anything.

leads.mechanism: The attributed unit cost is the controllable share of the real bill: model mix and case-volume decisions move attribution first, and the next window's billed spend follows it.
leads.lead_time: days — the cost report lands daily; attribution moves the day a run is taken

rejected.name: Runs per week
rejected.reason: Counts how often a human chose to measure, not whether the systems are good; its information lives in freshness.

rejected.name: Regressions caught before merge
rejected.reason: The outcome the program exists for; the store carries no branch or PR and CI never writes.
rejected.proxy: A run with a failed gating characteristic followed within 7 days by a passing run of the same subject with a newer code_version: caught and fixed.
rejected.proxy_misses: Regressions nobody ran a suite on, fixes by revert, and prompt-only fixes on the same code_version.

rejected.name: Time-to-green
rejected.reason: The same fail→pass pairing as the caught-and-fixed proxy, reported as days.

rejected.name: Gating coverage (gating cases per subject, advisory share)
rejected.reason: The pass rate's Goodhart counter; it travels with the outcome by rule and does not take a slot.

rejected.name: Advisory degradation rate
rejected.reason: Plausible mechanism, not a shown one; parked as a drill-through hypothesis until tracked data shows an advisory slip preceding a gating failure.

rejected.name: Overall mean pass rate across subjects
rejected.reason: Hides the failing repo; the program-level minimum is the honest aggregate.

rejected.name: Hallucination rate
rejected.reason: Only subjects reporting claims_checked carry it; inside the pass rate at program level.

rejected.name: Judge/human agreement
rejected.reason: The harness validates its judge in code; there is no run row to compute it from.

rejected.name: Trend-page freshness
rejected.reason: If it slips the fix is 'run the script', not a sponsor decision.

rejected.name: Unmeasured code-version drift, per subject
rejected.reason: Amended out 2026-08-25 (RC1-308): the instrument stage rejected it — released-but-never-measured consumer versions are not visible from any snapshot source; the store only ever sees versions someone chose to run.

notes: Adopted set per docs/kpi/trees/eval-run-store.review.md (2026-08-22): outcomes from the baseline (case-weighted; the agent's no-signal state and token×price fallback adopted); unmeasured-code-versions from the agent pending source verification in RC1-303; cost-per-run-by-model is the agent's outcome, demoted.

Amended by hand 2026-08-25 (RC1-308): real-cost-per-run added as the economics outcome on the real billing feeds; cost-per-verified-case demoted to leading (attribution leads the bill); unmeasured-code-versions moved to rejected on the instrument stage's verdict; cost-per-run-by-model retargeted to the new outcome. See docs/kpi/trees/eval-run-store.review.md § Amendment.
